title: Model recognition from a presheaf interval and anodyne extensions
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a small ordinary category, $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathrm{Set})$, and $1$ its terminal presheaf. Let $I\in\mathcal P$ have sections $e_0,e_1:1\to I$ for which $\delta=(e_0,e_1):1\amalg1\to I$ is a monomorphism. Products, pushouts and colimits are those of presheaves. For maps $i:U\to V$ and $j:K\to L$ write $i\square j:(V\times K)\amalg_{U\times K}(U\times L)\to V\times L$. Let $\mathrm{An}$ be the weakly saturated closure of a small set of monomorphisms; weak saturation means closure under isomorphisms, pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Assume $e_\varepsilon\square j\in\mathrm{An}$ for every monomorphism $j$ and $\varepsilon=0,1$, and $\delta\square i\in\mathrm{An}$ for every $i\in\mathrm{An}$. Say $Z$ is naive fibrant when $Z\to1$ has the right diagonal-lifting property against $\mathrm{An}$. A right lifting property means existence of a diagonal in each commutative square. Let $[K,Z]_I$ be $\operatorname{Hom}(K,Z)$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by pairs which are the two restrictions of a map $K\times I\to Z$. Let $W_I$ consist of those $u:K\to L$ inducing bijections $[L,Z]_I\to[K,Z]_I$ for every naive fibrant $Z$ in the input universe.

There is a cofibrantly generated model structure on $\mathcal P$ with monomorphisms as cofibrations, $W_I$ as weak equivalences, and fibrations the maps lifting against all monomorphisms in $W_I$. Its fibrant objects are exactly the naive fibrant objects, and every map in $\mathrm{An}$ is a trivial cofibration. Explicitly, $W_I$ contains isomorphisms, has two-out-of-three and is retract closed; the pairs (cofibrations, fibrations in $W_I$) and (cofibrations in $W_I$, fibrations) are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system has a factorization of every arrow and its two classes are exactly each other's left and right diagonal-lifting classes. Both systems are generated by small sets, and the constructions and factorizations stay in the input universe.

source.place: Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, July 30, 2026, Example 2.4.10 (product with an interval is an exact cylinder), Definition 2.4.11 (An0-An2), Definition 2.4.18 and Theorem 2.4.19, printed pp. 52-57; Proposition 2.4.25 (anodyne maps are weak equivalences), Remark 2.4.22 and Proposition 2.1.9 for functorial small-object factorizations. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. This generic theorem is proved in Section 2.4 before the construction of the Joyal model category, without a rigidification or Joyal input.
